title: Normalization of the derived group-restriction mate
statement:
Fix the small coherent profinite site and a coefficient universe containing its objects, morphisms and all section sets below [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $\mathcal M_R$ be its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and let $J,H$ be topological groups. Write $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$ and $\mathcal A_R(J)$ for internal $R$-modules with a natural $\underline J$-action by linear automorphisms [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the normalized functors of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants]: $T_J$ is trivial inflation, $\Gamma_{R,J}$ is the invariant subsheaf with its specified inclusion, $L_J=D(T_J)$, $F_J=R\Gamma_{R,J}$ with its canonical computation unit $\alpha_J$, and $L_J\dashv F_J$ is the canonical derived adjunction, with unit $\eta_J$ and counit $\varepsilon_J$. For a continuous homomorphism $u:H\to J$ put $U=D(u^*)$.

The mate
$$\beta_{u,N}=F_H(U\varepsilon_{J,N})\circ\eta_{H,F_JN}:F_JN\longrightarrow F_HUN$$
is the canonical total-derived transformation $b_u$ induced by the fixed-section inclusion $\iota_u:\Gamma_{R,J}\to\Gamma_{R,H}u^*$. More precisely its transpose is $U\varepsilon_{J,N}$, and for every complex $P$, with $Q$ denoting localization and $C(-)$ termwise application, it satisfies
$$\beta_{u,QP}\circ\alpha_{J,P}=\alpha_{H,C(u^*)P}\circ Q(C(\iota_u)_P),$$
under the canonical exact-localization identifications. The unbounded $F_J,F_H$ preserve $D^+$, and their restrictions with their computation units identify with the bounded-below right derived functors $(\mathbf R\Gamma_{R,J},\alpha)$, $(\mathbf R\Gamma_{R,H},\alpha)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]; the restricted adjunctions are the bounded-below derived adjunctions whose counit at a bounded-below complex $P$ of injectives is the class of the termwise counit $T_J\Gamma_{R,J}P\to P$ under these identifications. Thus if $P\to I$ and $u^*I\to I'$ are bounded-below injective resolutions, $\beta$ is represented by $\Gamma_{R,J}I\to\Gamma_{R,H}u^*I\to\Gamma_{R,H}I'$ with the specified computation-unit identifications.

This natural transformation commutes with the fixed shifts and gives a morphism on the two image triangles, including the last arrow: for $A\to B\to C\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1]$,
$$b_{u,A}[1]\circ F_J(\delta)=F_HU(\delta)\circ b_{u,C}$$
after the canonical shift comparisons. Under the computation-unit-normalized identifications $H^0F_J(M[0])=\Gamma_{R,J}M$, its degree-zero map is precisely $\iota_{u,M}$. For the identity homomorphism of a trivial group, $b_u$ is the identity under the identity restriction comparison.

proof.text:
Write $e_J:T_J\Gamma_{R,J}\to\mathrm{id}$ for the underived counit. The given $u:H\to J$ is a continuous group homomorphism, so postcomposition $C(S,u)$ preserves identity and multiplication on every test object. Hence precomposing a $J$-action gives an $H$-action. Restriction leaves modules and maps unchanged, so $u^*T_J=T_H$. A section fixed after every base change under $J$ is fixed under $H$, since $h$ acts through $u(h)$. Thus $\iota_u$ is the literal inclusion, natural in the equivariant module. The normalized transpose formulas give
$$e_{H,u^*M}\circ T_H(\iota_{u,M})=u^*(e_{J,M}).$$
Both sides send an invariant section to that same section. The equality holds termwise on complexes. Exactness of $T_J,T_H,u^*$ and the existence of the normalized derived adjunctions and computation units are supplied by the injective-infrastructure node. In all formulas below use the exact-localization comparison $UL_J=L_H$.

We first pin down the counit against the computation unit, for either group $G$. Exactness of $T_G$ permits the entire homotopy category as the left resolving class in the normalized derived-adjunction lemma. Choose a K-injective resolution $s:P\to I$. For the chain map $C(T_G\Gamma_{R,G})(P)\xrightarrow{e_{G,P}}P\xrightarrow{s}I$, its ordinary transpose is $C(\Gamma_{R,G})(s)$. The termwise-adjunction and resolving-normalization nodes therefore give its derived transpose as $\alpha_{G,I}\circ Q(C(\Gamma_{R,G})(s))=F_G(Qs)\circ\alpha_{G,P}$, the equality being naturality of $\alpha_G$. Transposing back gives
$$Qs\circ Q(e_{G,P})=\varepsilon_{G,QI}\circ L_G(F_G(Qs))\circ L_G(\alpha_{G,P}).$$
Naturality of $\varepsilon_G$ makes the right side $Qs\circ\varepsilon_{G,QP}\circ L_G(\alpha_{G,P})$. Cancel the isomorphism $Qs$ to obtain, for every complex,
$$\varepsilon_{G,QP}\circ L_G(\alpha_{G,P})=Q(e_{G,P}).$$

The mate formula with the identity comparison $UL_J=L_H$ makes $\beta$ natural and gives transpose $U\varepsilon_J$. Transpose the proposed computation-unit equation under $L_H\dashv F_H$. Its left side has transpose $U\varepsilon_{J,QP}\circ L_H(\alpha_{J,P})=UQ(e_{J,P})$, by step 2. Its right side has transpose
$$\varepsilon_{H,UQP}\circ L_H(\alpha_{H,C(u^*)P})\circ L_H Q(C(\iota_u)_P)=Q(e_{H,C(u^*)P})\circ L_H Q(C(\iota_u)_P),$$
again by step 2. These agree by step 1. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the equation. The total-right-derived universal property says a transformation from $F_J$ to $F_HU$ is uniquely determined by its composite with $\alpha_J$. Consequently this $\beta$ is exactly the total-derived inclusion $b_u$ with its specified normalization.

source.place: Tag 09T5; agent mate calculation, using the total-right-derived universal property.

proof.text: Apply the additive unbounded/bounded-below comparison lemma to $\Gamma_{R,G}$ for $G=J,H$. Its hypotheses hold by the infrastructure node: the source and target are abelian, the source has enough injectives and K-injective resolutions, and the invariant functor is additive. It gives preservation of $D^+$ and the unique comparison $\theta_G:F_G|_{D^+}\simeq R^+\Gamma_{R,G}$ satisfying $\theta_G\alpha_G=\alpha_G^+$. These are precisely the bounded-below pairs in the item. Since exact $T_G$ preserves cohomology and bounded-below complexes, $L_G$ also preserves $D^+$. The bounded-below categories are full, so the ambient Hom bijections restrict to an adjunction; their units and counits are the restrictions of the ambient ones. At a bounded-below injective complex $I$, step 2 and invertibility of $\alpha_{G,I}$ identify its counit with $Q(e_{G,I})$. Thus this restricted adjunction has the required bounded-below normalization.

Let $P\xrightarrow{s}I$ and $C(u^*)I\xrightarrow{t}I'$ be the two bounded-below injective resolutions. The comparison lemma computes $F_J(QP)$ by $Q\Gamma_{R,J}I$ and $F_H(UQP)$ by $Q\Gamma_{R,H}I'$, with the specified computation units. Step 3 at $I$ gives $\beta_{u,QI}\alpha_{J,I}=\alpha_{H,C(u^*)I}Q(C(\iota_u)_I)$. Compose with $F_H(Qt)$; naturality of $\alpha_H$ replaces $F_H(Qt)\alpha_{H,C(u^*)I}$ by $\alpha_{H,I'}Q(C(\Gamma_{R,H})(t))$. Cancel the invertible computation units at $I,I'$ and use naturality of $\beta$ along $Qs$. The representing map is exactly
$$\Gamma_{R,J}I\xrightarrow{\iota_u}\Gamma_{R,H}C(u^*)I\xrightarrow{\Gamma_{R,H}(t)}\Gamma_{R,H}I'.$$
This uses a separate target resolution; it requires no assertion that $u^*$ preserves injectives or K-injectives.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 070J; agent substitution in the computation-unit equation.

proof.text: The infrastructure node gives triangulated $F_J,F_H$, exact localized $U$, and shift-compatible derived units and counits. Hence the whiskered unit followed by the whiskered counit defining $\beta$ commutes with the fixed shifts, by the composition/whiskering lemma. For every arrow $f:X\to Y$, naturality gives $F_HU(f)b_{u,X}=b_{u,Y}F_J(f)$. Apply this to each arrow of $A\to B\to C\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1]$. For the last arrow it gives $F_HU(\delta)b_{u,C}=b_{u,A[1]}F_J(\delta)$; replace $b_{u,A[1]}$ by $b_{u,A}[1]$ using the shift compatibility just established. This is the stated last square after the canonical shift comparisons, and all four squares form the claimed morphism of image triangles.

source.place: Tags 014V (definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories), 014Y (lemma-composition-exact); agent application to the mate.

proof.text: The fixed-section formula shows directly that invariants preserve kernels: a section of $\ker(\Gamma d)$ is precisely a section in $\ker d$ fixed after every base change. The invariant functor is therefore left exact and additive. Apply the degree-zero injective-resolution lemma to $M$ and $\Gamma_{R,G}$. For a nonnegative injective resolution $M[0]\to I$ it identifies $\Gamma_{R,G}M$ with $H^0(\Gamma_{R,G}I)$ by the actual augmentation. The total-derived computation and its computation-unit-normalized bounded-below comparison identify this with $H^0F_G(M[0])$; hence $H^0\alpha_{G,M[0]}$ is exactly that identification. Take $H^0$ of the equation in step 3 for $P=M[0]$. Cancelling these identifications leaves $H^0 b_u=\iota_{u,M}$, as required.

proof.text: For an identity homomorphism, the specified restriction comparison is the identity on underlying modules and hence on localized complexes. The formula becomes $\beta_N=F_J(\varepsilon_{J,N})\circ\eta_{J,F_JN}=\mathrm{id}_{F_JN}$ by the adjunction triangle identity. This proves the requested trivial-group identity case (and in fact the same statement for every group).
